info.name: Invoice Reservation — Program Capacity
info.description:
Every request in this collection asserts what it expects, so **Run collection** exercises the
whole service and reports pass/fail.

### Before you start

```bash
docker compose --profile app up -d --build
```

Nothing else is needed: the collection mints its own bearer tokens from `jwtSecret`, which
matches the secret the Docker stack runs with. Point `baseUrl` elsewhere and set `jwtSecret`,
`jwtIssuer` and `jwtAudience` to match if you are testing another environment.

Requests run in order and share state — the first one opens a program with a fresh id each run,
and later ones reserve against it — so run the collection top to bottom rather than one request
in isolation.

### What it covers

- opening a program, and the same request repeated (idempotency)
- reserving capacity in the program currency and in another currency (FX conversion)
- partial and full repayments, including replays and misuse of a repayment id
- paging through reservations with a cursor
- every refusal: insufficient capacity, validation, 401, 403

The Kafka treasury feed is not HTTP, so it is not in here — see the README for
`npm run treasury`.

exec: const payload = encode({ iss: issuer, aud: audience, iat: now, exp: now + 3600, ...claims });
pm.collectionVariables.set("token", sign({ sub: "postman", scope: everything, programs: "*" }));
pm.collectionVariables.set("writerToken", sign({ sub: "postman-writer", scope: "capacity:read capacity:write", programs: "*" }));
// Same token with the signature broken, for the request that expects it to be refused.
